utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Are the interpreters and booths ready?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case IT-95-4-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal versus Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic aka "Krkan", Milojica Kos aka "Krle", Momcilo Gruban aka "Ckalja", Zdravko Govedarica, Gruban, Predrag Kostic aka "Kole," Nedeljko Paplalj, Milan Pavlic, Milutin Popovic, Drazenko Predojevic, Zeljko Savic, Mirko Babic, Nikica Janjic, Dusan Knezevic aka "Duca", Dragomir Saponja, Zoran Zigic aka "Ziga".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, more specifically today?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We have two accused here present -- Miroslav Kvocka and Mladen Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, please have Mr Mladen Radic and Miroslav Kvocka brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You may be seated. Mr Kvocka and Mr Radic, can you hear me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: In that case, please let us continue with this initial appearance hearing. I turn to the Office of the Prosecutor, who is appearing on behalf of the Prosecution today, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, your Honour. For the Prosecution I am Michael Keegan, I am assisted my by my colleagues, Mr Kapila Waidyaratne and Mr James Cowles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: For the Defence, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. My name is Tom Moran. I represent Mr Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: My name is Michael Greaves. I appear on behalf of the defendant Kvocka today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In order to begin this hearing of an initial appearance, I should like each one of the accused to spell his name -- first name, place and date of birth, occupation, and their last place of residence -- Mr Miroslav Kvocka, will you please tell us this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KVOCKA
utterances.text: My name is Miroslav Kvocka. I was born 1 January 1957 in Krijava in the Prijedor municipality. I am a policeman by profession -- professional policeman and the last residence is in Prijedor, Milos Oblica Street, number 46.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr Mladen Radic, will you answer the same questions, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: My name is Radic Mladen. I was born on 15 May 1952 in the village of Gornja Lamovita in Prijedor municipality. My last residence is King Aleksandar 36 and I am a policeman by profession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are going to continue with the proceedings of the initial appearance hearing. The Statute and our Rules require that I ask each one of you, Mr Kvocka and Mr Radic, to tell me who your Defence counsel is. Mr Kvocka, will you tell me who is your Defence counsel, who is your lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KVOCKA
utterances.text: The gentleman who just introduced himself a moment ago to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you. And as for you, Mr Radic, who is your attorney?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: Also the gentleman who just introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As this is a public hearing, I address myself to the public. An initial appearance has as its principal objective to verify before the Tribunal that the indictment has been clearly interpreted to the accused, and the conditions which led to the confirmation of the same indictment when it was confirmed by a judge of the Tribunal. We are respecting our founding documents, that is, the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal, founded in 1993, and the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Before reading the pertinent Articles of these texts, I also wish to say, in order to respect the public character of the audience and in order that everything be quite clear, that normally we are three judges here present, but the Rules, in accordance with Article 15 of the Statute, do envisage the possibility of the President of the Tribunal making an exception in the event that one or two of the judges are unable to present themselves today, that is, to be here with me, which is the case. Madam Registrar, could you please read Article 20(3) and 21(4)(a) and 62 and 62(B) of the Rules, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Article 20, paragraph 3 of the Statute: "The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy itself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment and instruct the accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber shall then set the date for trial." Article 21 of the Statute of the International Tribunal, paragraph (4)(a): "The accused shall be entitled in full equality to the following minimum guarantees: to be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and cause of the charge against him." Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence: "Upon his transfer to the seat of the Tribunal, the accused shall be brought before a Trial Chamber without delay and shall be formally charged. The Trial Chamber shall satisfy itself that the right of the accused to counsel is respected, read or have the indictment read to the accused in a language he speaks and understands, and satisfy itself that the accused understands the indictment; call upon the accused to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count; should the accused fail to do so, enter a plea of not guilty on his behalf. In case of a plea of not guilty, instruct the Registrar to set a date for trial. In case of a plea of guilty, instruct the Registrar to set a date for the pre-sentencing hearing; instruct the Registrar to set such other dates as appropriate." Article 62 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence: "If an accused pleads guilty in conformity with paragraph 5 of Rule 62, and if the Trial Chamber considers that the plea of guilty was done deliberately and is unequivocal, and that there is sufficient evidence to establish the crime and the participation of the accused in the crime, in the event of disagreement the Trial Chamber can enter in the record that the accused has pleaded guilty and fix the date for the pre-sentencing hearing."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I now turn to the Defence counsel, the indictment which I think you are familiar with has been conveyed to the accused. Have you explained to the accused the contents of the indictment? My question is addressed to Mr Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: My client has received a copy from the Registry whilst at Scheveningen of the indictment. I have discussed briefly the contents of that indictment with him, having had only an hour to talk to him today. I intend to discuss it with him further tomorrow. That will not be a problem today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr Moran?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: My client also received a copy of the indictment in Serbian. We have discussed it and he had no questions of me. However, I will also attempt to meet with him tomorrow to discuss it in further detail. It will not be a problem with proceeding today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. I will now ask the Registrar to proceed with the reading of the indictment concerning the two accused who are here present today. Therefore, Madam Registrar, will you please read the integral text of the indictment, the background, and the general allegations, and then the specific counts applicable to the two accused. Madam Registrar, will you please read the indictment issued by the International Criminal Tribunal against Miroslav Kvocka and Mladen Radic -- I apologise for the pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The indictment confirmed on 13 February 1995: the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia against Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic aka "Krkan", Milojica Kos aka "Krle", Momcilo Gruban aka "Ckalja", Zdravko Govedarica, Gruban, Predrag Kostic aka "Kole," Nedeljko Paplalj, Milan Pavlic, Milutin Popovic, Drazenko Predojevic, Zeljko Savic, Mirko Babic, Nikica Janjic, Dusan Knezevic aka "Duca", Dragomir Saponja, Zoran Zigic aka "Ziga". Richard J Goldstone, Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to his authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia charges: 1. From about 25 May to about 30 August 1992, Serb forces collected and confined more than 3,000 Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats from the opstina of Prijedor, Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the former Yugoslavia, in inhumane conditions under armed guard in the Omarska "camp", located in a former mining complex approximately 15 kilometres from the town of Prijedor. As set forth below, the Serb forces killed, raped, sexually assaulted, beat and otherwise mistreated the prisoners at Omarska. 2.1 In May 1992, intensive shelling of Muslim areas in the opstina of Prijedor caused the Muslim residents to flee their homes. The majority of them then surrendered or were captured by Serb forces. As the Serb forces rounded up the Muslims and any Croat residents, they forced the Muslims and Croats to march in columns bound for one or another of the prison camps that the Serbs had established in the opstina. The Serb forces pulled many of the Muslims and Croats from the columns and shot or beat them on the spot. 2.2 On about 25 May 1992, about three weeks after Serbs forcibly took control of government authority in the opstina, and two days after the start of large-scale military attacks on Muslim population centres, the Serb forces began taking prisoners to the Omarska camp. 2.3 During the next several weeks, the Serb forces continued to round up Muslims and Croats from Kozarac, Prijedor town, and other places in the opstina and interned them in the camps. Many of Prijedor's Muslim and Croat intellectuals, professional and political leaders were sent to Omarska. There were approximately 40 women in the camp and all the other prisoners in the camp were men. 2.4 Within the area of the Omarska mining complex that was used for the camp, the camp authorities generally confined the prisoners in three different buildings: the administration building, where interrogations took place and most of the women were confined; the garage or hangar building; the "white house", a small building where particularly severe beatings were administered; and on a cement courtyard area between the buildings known as the "pista". There was another small building known as the "red house" where prisoners were sometimes taken but most often did not emerge alive. 2.5 Living conditions at Omarska camp were brutal. Prisoners were crowded together with little or no facilities for personal hygiene. They were fed starvation rations once a day and given only three minutes to get into the canteen area, eat and get out. The little water they received was ordinarily foul. Prisoners had no changes of clothing and no bedding. They received no medical care. 2.6 Severe beatings were commonplace. The camp guards, and others who came to the camp and physically abused the prisoners, used all manner of weapons during these beatings, including wooden batons, metal rods and tools, lengths of thick industrial cable that had metal balls affixed to the end, rifle butts and knives. Both female and male prisoners were beaten, tortured, raped, sexually assaulted, and humiliated. In addition to regular beatings and abuse, there were incidents of multiple killings and special terror. Many whose identities are known and unknown, did not survive the camp. 3. The persons accused in this indictment were commanders, guards and others responsible for the conditions and mistreatment of prisoners in Omarska camp or otherwise assisted the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: 4. Zeljko Meakic also know as (hereinafter aka) Mejakic, aka Meagic, was in charge of Omarska camp beginning in late June, 1992, and was in a position of superior authority to everyone else in the camp. Before he took command of the camp, he was chief of security and had full authority over all the guards and any visitors. Before the war began in Bosnia-Herzegovina, he was a police official in the Omarska village. 5. Miroslav Kvocka and Dragoljub Prcac were deputies to Zeljko Meakic and were in positions of authority superior to everyone in the camp other than Meakic. For most of the first month of the camp's operation, Kvocka was the commander of the camp. Prior to the start of the war, both Kvocka and Prcac were officials at the Ministry of the Interior in Prijedor. 6. Mladen Radic aka Mlado Radic aka Krkan; Milojica Kos aka Krle; and Momcilo Gruban aka Ckalja were shift commanders who each supervised one of the three shifts of guards that operated at the camp. As shift commanders, when they were on duty, they were in positions of superior authority for all the camp personnel, second only to the camp commander and his deputies. 7. The following accused were among those who acted as guards in the Omarska camp: (a) Zdravko Govedarica, (b) first name unknown Gruban, (c) Predrag Kostic aka Kole, (d) Nedeljko Paspalj, (e) Milan Pavlic, (f) Milutin Popovic, (g) Drazenko Predojevic, (h) Zeljko Savic. 8. In addition to the above-listed accused, who regularly performed duties in Omarska camp, other Serbs entered the camp, subject to the authority of Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka and Dragoljub Prcac, where they killed, beat or otherwise physically abused prisoners. Among those who entered the camps were the following accused: (a) Mirko Babic, (b) Nikica Janjic,

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic aka Ziga. 9. At all times relevant to this indictment, a state of armed conflict and partial occupation existed in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. 10. All acts or omissions set forth as grave breaches recognised by Article 2 of the Statute of the Tribunal occurred during that armed conflict and partial occupation. 11. All of the prisoners at the Omarska camp, and the Bosnian Muslims and Croats of the opstina of Prijedor referred to in this indictment were, at all relevant times, persons protected by the Geneva Conventions of 1949. 12. All of the accused in this indictment were required to abide by the mandate of the laws and customs governing the conduct of war, including the Geneva Conventions of 1949. 13. Unless otherwise set forth below, all acts and omissions set forth in this indictment took place between 24 May and 30 August 1992. 14. In each paragraph charging torture, the acts were committed by, or at the instigation of, or with the consent or acquiescence of, an official or person acting in an official capacity, and for one or more of the following purposes: to obtain information or a confession from the victim or a third person; to punish the victim for an act the victim or a third person committed or was suspected of having committed; to intimidate or coerce the victim or a third person; and/or for any reason based upon discrimination of any kind. 15. In each paragraph charging crimes against humanity, a crime recognised by Article 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal, the alleged acts or omissions were part of a widespread or large-scale or systematic attack directed against a civilian population, specifically the Muslim and Croat population of the Prijedor district. 16. Paragraphs 4 through 15 are realleged and incorporated into each of the charges described below. 17. The term "Serb" refers either to Bosnian citizens of Serbian descent or to individuals for whom it is unknown whether they were Bosnian Serbs or citizens of Serbia proper. Paragraphs 18.1 to 18.3 will not be read because they apply exclusively to Zeljko Meakic. 19.1 With respect to the allegations in this indictment, Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban knew or had reason to know that persons in positions of subordinate authority to them at Omarska camp were about to commit those acts, or had already committed those acts, and failed to take the necessary and reasonable steps to prevent those acts or to punish the perpetrators after the acts had been committed. 19.2 During the operation of Omarska camp, camp guards and others who were subordinate to Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban regularly and openly killed, raped, tortured, beat, and otherwise subjected prisoners to conditions of constant humiliation, degradation and fear of death.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban in their capacities as superiors -- 19.3 Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the wilful killing of Omarska prisoners, including those described in paragraphs hereunder, grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 (hereinafter grave breaches) recognised by Articles 2(a) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or;. 19.4 Alternatively, Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the murder of Omarska prisoners, including those described in paragraphs hereunder, violations of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 19.5 Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the murder of Omarska prisoners, including those described in paragraphs hereunder, crimes against humanity recognised by Articles 5(a) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. 19.6 Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the torture of Omarska prisoners, grave breaches recognised by Articles 2(b) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or;. 19.7 Alternatively, Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the torture of Omarska prisoners, violations of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 19.8 Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the torture of Omarska prisoners, crimes against humanity recognised by Articles 5(f) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. 19.9 Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the rape of Omarska prisoners, including those described in paragraphs hereunder, crimes against humanity recognised by Articles 5(g) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. 19.10 Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in wilfully causing great suffering to Omarska prisoners, including those described in paragraphs hereunder, grave breaches recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal , or;. 19.11 Alternatively, Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the commission of outrages upon personal dignity, including humiliating and degrading treatment of the Omarska prisoners, violations of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(c) of the Geneva Conventions). 19.12 Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the unlawful confinement of civilians, including those listed in paragraphs hereunder, grave breaches recognised by Articles 2(g) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or;. 19.13 Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for their own acts or omissions and for the acts of their subordinates in the unlawful imprisonment of the prisoners of Omarska, including those listed in paragraphs hereunder, crimes against humanity recognised by Articles 5(e) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal). Paragraphs 20.1 through 20.4will not be read, because they only apply to the accused Zeljko Meakic. Accused: Mladen Radic. 22.1 During June and July, 1992, Mladen Radic repeatedly subjected "A" to forcible sexual intercourse. The first occasion was on or about the night of 25 June 1992. Mladen Radic took "A" to a room downstairs in the administration building, forced her on a table and subjected her to forcible sexual intercourse. Two or three nights later, Radic again called "A" out of the room where she slept and again subjected her to forcible sexual intercourse. On at least three more occasions during June and July 1992, Mladen Radic called "A" out of the room in the administration building where she slept and subjected her to forcible sexual intercourse. These crimes are charged separately below: First incident: 22.2 Around 25 June, 1992, Mladen Radic wilfully caused "A" great suffering her by subjecting her to forcible sexual intercourse, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal or; 22.3 Alternatively, around 25 June 1992, Mladen Radic subjected "A" to cruel treatment by forcible sexual intercourse, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 22.4 Around 25 June 1992, Mladen Radic raped "A", a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Second incident: 22.5 Around 27 June 1992, Mladen Radic wilfully caused "A" great suffering by subjecting her to forcible sexual intercourse, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 22.6 Alternatively, around 27 June 1992, Mladen Radic subjected "A" to cruel treatment by forcible sexual intercourse, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 22.7 Around 27 June 1992, Mladen Radic raped "A", a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Third incident: 22.8 During July, 1992, Mladen Radic wilfully caused "A" great suffering by subjecting her to forcible sexual intercourse, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 22.9 Alternatively, during July, 1992, Mladen Radic subjected "A" to cruel treatment by forcible sexual intercourse, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 22.10 During July, 1992, Mladen Radic raped "A", a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Fourth incident: 22.11 During late July, 1992, Mladen Radic wilfully caused "A" great suffering by subjecting her to forcible sexual intercourse, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 22.12 Alternatively, during late July, 1992, Mladen Radic subjected "A" to cruel treatment by forcible sexual intercourse, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 22.12 During late July, 1992, Mladen Radic raped "A", a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Fifth incident: 22.14 During late July, 1992, Mladen Radic wilfully caused "A" great suffering by subjecting her to forcible sexual intercourse, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 22.15 Alternatively, during late July 1992, Mladen Radic subjected "A" to cruel treatment by forcible sexual intercourse, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 22.16 During late July, 1992, Mladen Radic raped "A", a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Accused: Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic. 23.1 In about July 1992, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic and a third unknown person savagely beat Becir Medunjanin on two occasions over a two-day period in the "white house". The accused assaulted Becir Medunjanin with a club, a chair, a baton and kicked him. The morning after the second assault Becir Medunjanin died in the room and his body was removed from the camp immediately. 23.2 Zoran Zigic and Dusan Knezevic participated in the wilful killing of Becir Medunjanin, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or;. 23.3 Alternatively, Zoran Zigic and Dusan Knezevic participated in the murder of Becir Medunjanin, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 23.4 Zoran Zigic and Dusan Knezevic participated in the murder of Becir Medunjanin, a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. 24.1 On or about 10 June 1992, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic went to the Omarska camp. Zigic, Knezevic, Saponja and Janjic were not regular guards at the camp, but were allowed into the camp to murder, beat or otherwise physically abuse the prisoners. On that particular day, they called four prisoners at the Omarska camp, Emir Beganovic, Rezak Hukanovic, Asef Kapetanovic, and Sefik Terzic into the "white house", and severely beat them. The accused used metal batons and cables, a knife, their fists and kicked the victims with their military-style boots. Victim: Emir Beganovic 24.2 Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Emir Beganovic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or;. 24.3 Alternatively, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Emir Beganovic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 24.4 Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Emir Beganovic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Victim: Rezak Hukanovic 24.5 Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Rezak Hukanovic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal), or; 24.6 Alternatively, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Rezak Hukanovic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 24.7 Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Rezak Hukanovic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Victim: Asef Kapetanovic 24.8 Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Asef Kapetanovic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 24.9 Alternatively, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Asef Kapetanovic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 24.10 Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Asef Kapetanovic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Victim: Sefik Terzic 24.11 Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Sefik Terzic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 24.12 Alternatively, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Sefik Terzic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 24.13 Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Sefik Terzic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Accused: Gruban 25.1 Between early June and 3 August 1992, a guard at the Omarska camp with the surname Gruban, who was a member of Mladen Radic's shift, repeatedly forced "F" from the room where she was sleeping, took her to another room on the first floor of the administration building in the Omarska camp and subjected her to forcible sexual intercourse. 25.2 Gruban wilfully caused "F" great suffering by subjecting her to forcible sexual intercourse, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 25.3 Alternatively, Gruban subjected "F" to cruel treatment by forcible sexual intercourse, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 25.4 Gruban raped "F", a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Accused: Predrag Kostic aka Kole 26.1 Between early June and 3 August 1992, Predrag Kostic, a guard at the Omarska camp forced "F" from the room where she was sleeping, took her to another room on the first floor of the administration building in the Omarska camp and subjected her to forcible sexual intercourse. 26.2 Predrag Kostic aka Kole wilfully caused "F" great suffering by subjecting her to forcible sexual intercourse, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 26.3 Alternatively, Predrag Kostic aka Kole subjected "F" to cruel treatment by forcible sexual intercourse, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 26.4 Predrag Kostic aka Kole raped "F", a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Accused: Milutin Popovic, Drazenko Predojevic, Zeljko Savic and Nedeljko Paspalj 27.1 Around 6 July 1992, on the "pista", the victim Rizah Hadzalic, in response to a comment by a guard, used a common polite Bosnian expression, "Bujrum". The accused Milutin Popovic, together with the co-accused Drazenko Predojevic, Zeljko Savic, Nedeljko Paspalj and a guard known only as "Nedo" went to Rizah Hadzalic and beat him for using this Muslim expression. The four accused and "Nedo" beat Rizah Hadzalic until he fell to the ground in a sitting position. About half an hour later, Rizah Hadzalic died as a result of the beating. 27.2 Milutin Popovic, Drazenko Predojevic, Zeljko Savic and Nedeljko Paspalj participated in the wilful killing of Rizah Hadzalic, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 27.3 Alternatively, Milutin Popovic, Drazenko Predojevic, Zeljko Savic and Nedeljko Paspalj participated in the murder of Rizah Hadzalic, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 27.4 Milutin Popovic, Drazenko Predojevic, Zeljko Savic and Nedeljko Paspalj participated in the murder of Rizah Hadzalic, a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Accused: Milan Pavlic 28.1 In early June, 1992, a large group of prisoners were confined in the canteen area of the administration building of the Omarska camp. One night an elderly man, Mehmedalija Nasic, stood up and shouted in apparent protest over the prisoners' confinement. He was, at the time, distressed and possibly mentally disturbed by the conditions that he had been forced to endure. The accused, Milan Pavlic, a regular guard at Omarska, ordered him to sit down. Nasic did not sit down, and after a few minutes Pavlic fired his rifle, killing the victim and wounding several other prisoners sitting nearby. 28.2 Milan Pavlic wilfully killed Mehmedalija Nasic, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 28.3 Alternatively, Milan Pavlic murdered Mehmedalija Nasic, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 28.4 Milan Pavlic murdered Mehmedalija Nasic, a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Zdravko Govedrica 29.1 On or about 17 June 1992, Zdravko Govedarica, a guard in the Omarska camp, with four other guards whose names are not known, took Serif Velic, a prisoner in the camp, to a room in the administration building where they stripped him to his underwear, kicked him in the testicles, repeatedly beat him with a baton and rifle, and kicked him in the ribs, causing him to lapse in and out of consciousness. 29.2 Zdravko Govedarica wilfully subjected Serif Velic to great suffering, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 29.3 Alternatively, Zdravko Govedarica subjected Serif Velic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 29.4 Zdravko Govedarica subjected Serif Velic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(i) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Mirko Babic 30.1 "F" was taken to the Omarska camp as a prisoner in early June 1992. Sometime between early June and 3 August 1992, "F" was taken to the Separcija building at the entrance to the Omarska camp and placed in a room where Mirko Babic subjected "F" to forcible sexual intercourse. 30.2 Mirko Babic wilfully caused great suffering to "F" by subjecting her to forcible sexual intercourse, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 30.3 Alternatively, Mirko Babic subjected "F" to cruel treatment by forcible sexual intercourse, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. 30.4 Mirko Babic raped "F", a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Accused: Dusan Knezevic 31.1 Around the latter part of June or the first part of July 1992, near the building known as the "white house", a group of Serbs from outside the camp, including Dusan Knezevic, ordered prisoners whose names are not known, to drink water like animals from puddles on the ground, jumped on their backs and beat them until they were unable to move. As the victims were removed in a wheelbarrow, one of the Serbs discharged the contents of a fire extinguisher into the mouth of one of the victims. 31.2 Dusan Knezevic participated in wilfully causing a group of Omarska prisoners, whose names are not known, great suffering or serious injury to body or health, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 31.3 Alternatively, Dusan Knezevic participated in subjecting these unknown Omarska prisoners to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 31.4 Dusan Knezevic participated in subjecting these unknown Omarska prisoners to inhuman acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Signed, Richard J Goldstone, Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I now turn to the accused. Will you please rise? Mr Kvocka first, have you understood well the meaning of this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KVOCKA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Have you understood in your mother tongue -- have you heard it in your mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KVOCKA
utterances.text: Yes, I did in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, you may be seated, Mr Kvocka. Mr Radic, I ask you the same question: have you heard the indictment? Have you understood it in your mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, you may be seated. I am now going to ask you, and I turn to the accused -- I am going to ask you to make a plea of guilty or not guilty to the various counts with which you are charged by the Office of the Prosecutor. For that purpose, I am going to ask Madam Registrar to read the counts that apply to you and, after each one of these, you will tell me simply whether you have chosen, in agreement with your Defence counsel, to plead guilty or, the opposite, not guilty. The consequences in terms of the trial are different, as you know. Your attorneys should have indicated these differences to you. Therefore, Mr Kvocka and Mr Radic, this brings us to your counts and will you please devote full attention to them? After each of the counts have been read out -- each of the charges -- which will be read by Madam Registrar, will you please plead guilty or not guilty. Madam Registrar, you may now read the charges against Mr Miroslav Kvocka, please. I beg your pardon, will Mr Kvocka rise, please. You may continue, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraphs 19.3 and 19.4: Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the wilful killing of Omarska prisoners, including those described in paragraphs hereunder, grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 (hereinafter grave breaches) recognised by Articles 2(a) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 19.4 Alternatively, Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the murder of Omarska prisoners, including those described in paragraphs hereunder, violations of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr Kvocka, do you plead guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KVOCKA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, please register the plea of "not guilty" and please announce the next charge.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.text: Mr Miroslav Kvocka, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The charges contained in paragraphs 19.6 and 19.7 are put alternatively -- 19.6 therefore: Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the torture of Omarska prisoners, grave breaches recognised by Articles 2(b) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 19.7 Alternatively, Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the torture of Omarska prisoners, violations of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr Kvocka, do you plead guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KVOCKA
utterances.text: No, your Honour, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you may continue.

utterances.text: 19.8: Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the torture of Omarska prisoners, crimes against humanity recognised by Articles 5(f) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr Kvocka, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. KVOCKA

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraphs 19.12 and 19.13 contain charges in the alternative: Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the unlawful confinement of civilians, including those listed in paragraphs hereunder, grave breaches recognised by Articles 2(g) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 19.13 Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for their own acts or omissions and for the acts of their subordinates in the unlawful imprisonment of the prisoners of Omarska, including those listed in paragraphs hereunder, crimes against humanity recognised by Articles 5(e) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr Kvocka, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. KVOCKA
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Therefore, Madam Registrar, will you please take note of the not guilty plea of Mr Kvocka in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You may be seated, Mr Kvocka. Mr Mladen Radic, will you please rise? The Prosecutor is charging you with the charges appearing in the indictment. I am going to ask you, too, in the same way that I have done in the case of Mr Kvocka, whether you plead guilty or not guilty. Madam Registrar, can you please read out the first charge against Mr Radic, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.3 and paragraph 19.4 are put in the alternative: Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the wilful killing of Omarska prisoners, including those described in paragraphs hereunder, grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 (hereinafter grave breaches) recognised by Articles 2(a) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal); or, 19.4 Alternatively, Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic, Milojica Kos and Momcilo Gruban are criminally responsible for the acts of their subordinates in the murder of Omarska prisoners, including those described in paragraphs hereunder, violations of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES

utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraphs 22.11 and 22.12 of the indictment are put in the alternative. 22.11 During late July 1992, Mladen Radic wilfully caused "A" great suffering by subjecting her to forcible sexual intercourse, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 22.12 Alternatively, during late July 1992, Mladen Radic subjected "A" to cruel treatment by forcible sexual intercourse, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr Radic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraph 22.13: During late July 1992, Mladen Radic raped "A", a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr Radic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You may continue, madam.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraphs 22.14 and 22.15 of the indictment are put in the alternative. 22.14 During late July 1992, Mladen Radic wilfully caused "A" great suffering by subjecting her to forcible sexual intercourse, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 22.15 Alternatively, during late July 1992, Mladen Radic subjected "A" to cruel treatment by forcible sexual intercourse, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr Radic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Continue, madam.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraph 22.16: During late July 1992, Mladen Radic raped "A", a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr Radic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I should like to ask the Registrar to take note of the plea of not guilty of the two accused.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I now turn to the Prosecutor to remind him, as is usual, in the event of each initial appearance, of the obligation that he has to disclose all the supporting material with the indictment at the moment of the confirmation of the indictment, as well as the statements of the accused and the statements of witnesses. Mr Prosecutor, are you in a position to be able to disclose those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, we are prepared to do so prior to the hearing. We were not advised of who the counsel would be for the accused so we did not have the materials, but we will arrange to do so. I would also like to note for the record, on Thursday, 9 April, the Prosecutor submitted an application to the President of the Tribunal to have this case assigned to Trial Chamber II bis. A large part of the evidence to be presented with respect to these accused is also relevant to the case against Milan Kovacevic. In the interests of the victims and witnesses in those cases, for their security and consideration of the trauma caused by testimony, particularly in the case of sexual assault victims, we would seek to request a concurrent presentation of the evidence. It also will serve the interests of judicial economy. In the event that any additional accused from this indictment are arrested we would seek the same type of request with the President. As I am aware of, that request has not been moved upon yet, but I wanted to make the Trial Chamber aware of that request for planning purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr Prosecutor, have you requested a joinder of the trials, or simply that this case be tried by Trial Chamber II bis, which would mean that they would have two trials, or will there be just one combined trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: At this stage, your Honour, the request was, at this early stage, simply to have the case assigned to Trial Chamber II bis and then the mechanics of whether cases would be joined or whether they would merely be a concurrent presentation of evidence for the two cases would be something we would then take up with the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, just a moment, please, I will give you the floor in a minute, Mr Moran. If I have understood well, regarding the date, you are ready to disclose all the necessary documents and we could communicate to the Defence the date when the period shall begin to be counted for the pre-trial motions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, I should like to hear the Defence, also, on this point, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr Moran.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: As I am sure the court is familiar, Mr Greaves and I are at least right now on a temporary basis representing these two gentlemen. However, I think I speak for both Mr Greaves and myself to object to the Prosecutor's motion to send this to Trial Chamber II bis. I think there are two reasons for that. First, President McDonald signed an order, today sending it to Trial Chamber I. It seems that she has considered that and it is within her discretion. Secondly, we have an expression where I come from called "forum shopping" where lawyers will try to get cases for various reasons into a particular court. Where I come from -- I do not know where the practice is in other places -- it is considered to be improper conduct -- you get -- if you would, you get whatever forum the procedure normally calls for, understanding that different judges do different things differently. I do not think the Prosecutor should be allowed to engage in this kind of forum shopping. Finally, the procedure the Prosecutor seems to be asking for is something that would be incredibly difficult to do. I do not even know physically how one could go about this, given the constraints of this courtroom and, as I understand it, the two new courtrooms -- being involved in the Celebici case for as long as I have, I can tell you, your Honour, that it gets a little close over on this side of the room occasionally. For those reasons, I would ask that the court deny that request and in fact -- I am not real sure that this Trial Chamber should even be considering it. I think that is probably more a matter that should be taken up with Judge McDonald in her capacity as the President of the court. As for delivery of the discovery documents, I would ask that the discovery documents be delivered to counsel at the time that permanent counsel arrives. I would hate to take custody of several boxes of documents and then have something turn up missing. I would ask the court to delay that at least until Friday of this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, I think we are in agreement, but in any event, Mr Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That is fine with the Prosecution, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I think that we have covered all the questions relevant to an initial appearance. Before adjourning, I would like to address myself once again to Mr Kvocka and Mr Radic to hear whether they have any observations to make at this stage. Mr Kvocka, do you have any observations to make -- just Mr Kvocka, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KVOCKA
utterances.text: No, nothing, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: And you, Mr Radic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: No, I have no observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Then I think there is no other outstanding matter. Therefore, the question of the status conference will be dealt with later, but I think we can now rise. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: One matter I think that the court can deal with fairly promptly. If the usher could take this document -- it is a letter sent by me to the Prosecutor today on behalf of both myself and Mr Greaves asking that the investigators for the Office of the Prosecutor not contact either of these gentlemen without our presence or permission and until -- if in fact we are relieved, without the presence and permission of other counsel. It appears that there has been an attempt to interview one of the two defendants today and we would just ask for protective order from the court ordering the Prosecutor to go through counsel -- properly assigned counsel in order to change interviews with these men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, but the accused always have the right to be heard in the presence of attorneys and I am sure that the Prosecutor is going to respect that rule. You are familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, we were handed a copy of it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Our only request, your Honour, is that any attempt to arrange those interviews -- that the court order the Prosecutor to go through properly assigned counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes. We will take note of this request, but I do not really think it is necessary. But, in any event, we will take those measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned. Good afternoon everyone.
